title: Far-right support over time by ideology
estimand_or_content: Equal-country survey-wave mean far-right support by ideology in AIDs and LMICs; broad ideology definition
caption: Far-right vote share by ideological self-placement and survey wave. The main ideology definition classifies E033 scores 1-4 as Left, 5-6 as Moderate, and 7-10 as Right. Each point is an equal-country survey-wave mean after applying survey weights within country-surveys. AIDs include WVS and EVS observations; LMICs include WVS observations only. Far-right support is measured from respondents' party-choice or party-appeal responses: E179_WVS in WVS; E179 in EVS waves 1-4, with E181/E181A used as fallbacks where applicable; EVS wave 5 uses E181A.

title: Adjusted probability of far-right support by ideology
estimand_or_content: Country-fixed-effect LPM counterfactual-standardized probability of far-right support by ideology
caption: Counterfactual-standardized probabilities from a survey-weighted respondent-level linear probability model with country fixed effects and country-clustered standard errors. The ideology definition is Left 1-4, Moderate 5-6, and Right 7-10. Error bars are 95% confidence intervals. Moderate support exceeds Left support by 4.3 percentage points (95% CI 2.6 to 6.0); Right support exceeds Moderate support by 6.3 percentage points (95% CI 3.4 to 9.3).

title: BJP vote share by voter ideology, 2009 and 2014
estimand_or_content: Survey-weighted BJP vote share among audited Left, Center, and Right NES respondents in 2009 and 2014
caption: Survey-weighted BJP vote shares among respondents classified Left, Center, or Right in the National Election Studies. Mixed respondents are omitted from the bars. 2009: n=4,216 (11.5% of the full sample); 21.4% of Mixed respondents with valid reported votes voted BJP (weighted). 2014: n=10,464 (46.9% of the full sample); 34.4% voted BJP (weighted). 2009 classification: 2/2 recognition items + at least 2/3 statism items in the same bucket. 2014 classification: Q10b + Q10e + corrected Q23c all support the same bucket. Weights: stpop1 (2009) and stpop (2014).

title: Far-right support in India by ideology

title: Assembly-constituency models of centrist BJP support
estimand_or_content: Raw Total and Manufacturing FDI: additive, interaction without primary controls, and interaction with primary controls; state fixed effects and baseline FDI retained
caption: Assembly-constituency estimates of centrist BJP support in 2014. Columns 1-3 use Total local FDI and columns 4-6 use Manufacturing local FDI. Within each exposure family, the first column is additive, the second adds the Muslim-share interaction, and the third adds the primary constituency controls. All specifications retain baseline FDI and state fixed effects. Standard errors are clustered by parliamentary constituency.

title: Voter-level models of centrist BJP support
estimand_or_content: Unweighted centrist-voter LPMs for raw Total and Manufacturing FDI with AC random intercepts and state fixed effects
caption: Voter-level linear probability models of BJP voting among 2014 centrist respondents. Columns 1-3 use Total local FDI and columns 4-6 use Manufacturing local FDI. Within each exposure family, the first column is additive, the second adds the Muslim-share interaction, and the third adds the primary individual and constituency controls. All specifications retain baseline FDI, state fixed effects, and an assembly-constituency random intercept.

title: Manufacturing FDI and the Muslim-share gradient in centrist BJP support
estimand_or_content: Change in BJP support associated with a +1 percentage-point Muslim population share across current raw Manufacturing FDI
caption: Marginal effect of a one-percentage-point increase in Muslim population share across current Manufacturing FDI exposure. Panel A reports the assembly-constituency model and Panel B the voter-level model. The calculation incorporates the fitted current-FDI interaction while averaging the baseline-FDI contribution over the corresponding estimation sample. Shaded intervals are 95% confidence intervals. The x-axis reports raw Manufacturing FDI projects per 100,000 population.

title: Robustness of the FDI × Muslim-share relationship
estimand_or_content: Reference-standardized change in the +1-pp Muslim-share BJP-support gradient associated with a one-SD increase in registered Total or Manufacturing FDI exposure
caption: Assembly-constituency robustness of the FDI × Muslim-share interaction across registered Total and Manufacturing FDI definitions. Effects are placed on a common scale using the Primary-sample reference standard deviation for each exposure family. Primary and Expanded control sets are shown separately. The 12-month temporal-window specifications are post-estimation robustness checks rather than part of the original primary specification.
